headword: {発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}

definitions.explanation: Food products that have been transformed through the action of microorganisms such as bacteria, yeast, or mold. Includes items like miso, soy sauce, natto, yogurt, and kimchi.

examples.japanese: {納豆|なっとう}は{代表的|だいひょうてき}な{発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}だ。
examples.english: Natto is a typical fermented food.

examples.japanese: {発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}は{腸内環境|ちょうないかんきょう}を{整|ととの}えると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Fermented foods are said to improve gut health.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{味噌|みそ}、{醤油|しょうゆ}、{漬|つ}け{物|もの}など{多|おお}くの{発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}があり、{和食|わしょく}に{欠|か}かせない{存在|そんざい}だ。
examples.english: Japan has many fermented foods such as miso, soy sauce, and pickles, which are essential to Japanese cuisine.

notes:
CULTURE:
Japan has a particularly rich tradition of fermented foods. Key examples include {味噌|みそ} (miso), {醤油|しょうゆ} (soy sauce), {納豆|なっとう} (natto), {漬|つ}け{物|もの} (pickles), {酢|す} (vinegar), and {甘酒|あまざけ} (sweet sake). Fermented foods have received increased attention for their health benefits.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}を{取|と}り{入|い}れる (to incorporate fermented foods)
- {伝統的|でんとうてき}な{発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん} (traditional fermented foods)
- {発酵食品|はっこうしょくひん}ブーム (fermented food boom)
